{{Short description|American physicist (born 1943)}}
'''Tom C. Lubensky''' (born Kansas City, Missouri 7 May 1943) is an American [[physicist]]. He is currently the Christopher H. Browne Distinguished Professor Emeritus at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], where he was Mary Amanda Wood professor of [[physics]] (1998–2009) and chair of the Department of Physics and Astronomy.<ref name="tl0">{{cite web | url=https://almanac.upenn.edu/archive/v45pdf/990126/012699.pdf | title=Mary Amanda Wood Chair: Dr. Tom Lubensky | publisher=www.upenn.edu|access-date=2009-07-23}}</ref><ref name="tl">{{cite web | url=http://www.mrsec.harvard.edu/fscm/lubensky.htm | title= Tom Lubensky Biography| publisher=www.mrsec.harvard.edu|accessdate=2009-07-22}}</ref>

==Biography==
Dr. Lubensky received his B.S. in physics from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1964 and both his M.A. (1965) and Ph.D. (1969) in physics from [[Harvard University]]. He was an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] Postdoctoral Fellow at the [[University of Paris]] in [[Orsay]] (1969–70) and a postdoctoral research associate at [[Brown University]] (1970–71). He joined the University of Pennsylvania in 1971, promoted to associate professor in 1975 and to full professor in 1980.<ref name="tl0"/>

==Memberships==
He is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (1985), [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2000), elected member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] (2002) and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2007), [[Sloan Fellows|Alfred P. Sloan Fellow]] (1975–77), [[Guggenheim Fellow]] (1981), and honored member of the [[International Liquid Crystal Society]].<ref name="tl1">{{cite web | url=http://www.physics.upenn.edu/people/t.lubensky.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080509191835/http://www.physics.upenn.edu/people/t.lubensky.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=May 9, 2008 | title= Tom C. Lubensky| publisher=www.physics.upenn.edu|accessdate=2009-07-22}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 2004 Dr. Lubensky received [[Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize]] for seminal contributions to the theory of condensed matter systems including the prediction and elucidation of the properties of new, partially ordered phases of complex materials.<ref name="tl3">{{cite web | url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?name=Tom%20Lubensky&year=2004 | title= 2004 Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize Recipient| publisher=[[American Physical Society|APS]]|accessdate=2009-07-22}}</ref> in 2024 he was awarded the de Gennes medal by the International Liquid Crystal Liquid Crystal Society for pioneering high-level scientific achievement in liquid crystals.

==Books==

Lubensky is the coauthor of the textbook ''Principles of Condensed Matter Physics''<ref>{{cite journal|author=Karakashian, A. S.|title=A Review of "Principles of Condensed Matter Physics" by PM Chaikin and TC Lubensky, Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, UK, 2000, {{text|ISBN}} 0 521 79450 1 (paperback)|year=2001|page=275|doi=10.1080/10587250108030023|journal=Molecular Crystals and Liquid Crystals Science and Technology. Section A. Molecular Crystals and Liquid Crystals|volume=369|issue=1|s2cid=96677269}}</ref> ({{ISBN|0-521-43224-3}}) with [[Paul Chaikin]].
